transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-22
Time: 14:00 - 14:46 UTC (46 minutes)
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Martins (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Redwood CSM); Priya Patel, Evan Ross, Nadia Kaur, Samir Joshi (Suncrest)

Summary:
Quick alignment on POC success criteria and a detailed quality evaluation plan: golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination/format checks, and scoring approach. Agreed to run a 1-week benchmark run with 500 sample clinical notes and a follow-up review.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Ava Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate the time. Quick intros?
[00:07] Priya Patel: Hi, I'm Priya, Director of AI at Suncrest. Evan here leads engineering, Nadia on privacy, Samir is ML lead.
[00:15] Ava Chen: Great, I have Diego from our Solutions Engineering team and Maya from success. I'll run goals for today's call: nail down what "success" looks like for the POC, workload sizing for benchmarks, and the concrete quality eval plan — golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination checks, scoring.
[00:30] Evan Ross: Sounds good. We're focused on triage note summarization and structured-field extraction from clinical notes. Latency matters but quality is top. Budget is TBD but we want clear unit economics.
[00:44] Diego Martins: Understood. A couple quick qualifiers: are you planning to run on hosted Redwood API or Private (VPC/on-prem)? That affects data flow and benchmark setup.
[00:54] Samir Joshi: For the POC we're okay with hosted sandbox if data is sanitized — but if there are any production plans, we'd need VPC. For now, hosted is fine, provided we can verify KMS controls and audit logs.
[01:06] Nadia Kaur: Correct, we need SOC2 compliance evidence and a mechanism for audit logs and RBAC. We'll review security pack.
[01:14] Ava Chen: We'll share SOC2 and SAML/SSO docs. Ok, on success criteria — what would you consider a win?
[01:21] Priya Patel: For summarization: ROUGE-like scores are useful, but clinically we care about factual accuracy (no hallucinations) and correct extraction of med lists, dosages. Numeric thresholds: precision/recall for extractions > 90% ideally, hallucination rate under 2% on critical entities, and average latency < 800ms per request at the expected load.
[01:41] Diego Martins: Good, that's actionable. We'll recommend targeted metrics: exact-match for structured fields, F1 for entity extraction, and a hallucination score computed by reference checks against golden outputs.
[01:52] Ava Chen: Timelines: we propose 1 week to prepare harness and golden prompts, then a 1-week benchmark run with your sample data, then a results review. Does that align?
[02:02] Evan Ross: Yes. We can get samples by next Monday.
[02:05] Ava Chen: Great. Now the quality eval plan — high-level: 1) Golden prompts and reference outputs; 2) Regression test suite that runs on each model variant; 3) Hallucination and format checks; 4) Scoring and dashboard for pass/fail and continuous monitoring. We'll walk through each.
[02:20] Diego Martins: Golden prompts: we'll define canonical prompts for each task — e.g., "Summarize the following triage note into a 2-3 sentence clinical summary" and prompt variants for brevity vs. detail. We ask customer to provide 50 golden examples with expected outputs (these don't have to be exhaustive but should cover edge cases).
[02:40] Priya Patel: We can provide 50 seed golden prompts plus 500 sample notes for the benchmark. We'll also annotate 100 of them with expected structured extraction outputs.
[02:50] Diego Martins: Perfect. Regression tests: two layers — unit/regression checks on the prompt-output mapping (deterministic or near-deterministic tests) and statistical regression tests across the batch for metrics like F1, exact match, hallucination rate, and formatting adherence (JSON schema). We'll run them per-model and across the rollout.
[03:10] Ava Chen: On hallucination checks: we'll run entity-level verification comparing extracted entities against reference lists; for summaries we'll flag statements that assert facts not present in the note using an NER/lookup pipeline and a lightweight contradiction detector. Note that this is imperfect but catches many false assertions.
[03:28] Samir Joshi: How do you score hallucinations? We need a concrete metric.
[03:32] Diego Martins: We propose a Hallucination Rate = (number of hallucinated assertions) / (total assertions) aggregated per document. Also a Critical Hallucination flag for entities like allergies, dosages, or diagnoses — those count heavier in the score. We can compute a weighted hallucination score: critical x3 weight.
[03:47] Priya Patel: That weighting makes sense. For format checks we want strict JSON output for structured fields — anything non-conformant is a test failure.
[03:56] Diego Martins: We'll provide a JSON schema and our runtime will validate outputs. We also have a fallback and repair routine if the model returns poorly formatted JSON: post-processing heuristics and a second-pass prompt to reformat.
[04:08] Evan Ross: For benchmarks, what throughput and latency should we use? Our production is ~50 concurrent requests with an average QPS of 10 and typical note length of 600 tokens.
[04:18] Diego Martins: For the POC harness we'll emulate a representative workload: batch sizes and concurrency matching your production: 50 concurrent clients, QPS 10 sustained, and a 2x burst test. We'll run per-model latency p95 and p99, plus token-level cost estimates.
[04:33] Ava Chen: Success criteria recap: extraction F1 >= 0.9, hallucination rate < 2% overall and <1% critical, p95 latency < 800ms under target load, format pass rate > 98%. If we meet those, POC considered successful. Any objections?
[04:49] Priya Patel: No objections; maybe add qualitative clinician review for 20 samples to confirm clinical acceptability.
[04:56] Ava Chen: Agree — we'll include a clinician QA pass for 20 random notes and include their pass/fail notes in the report.
[05:03] Diego Martins: Scoring approach: we'll produce a combined scorecard per-task. Example fields: ExactMatch%, F1, HallucinationRate (weighted), FormatPassRate, LatencyP95, CostPerDoc. We'll compute a normalized score 0-100 and mark pass/fail per threshold.
[05:20] Samir Joshi: How do we handle model variants and rollouts?
[05:23] Diego Martins: We'll test 3 variants: full-precision baseline, quantized-8 variant, and fast-low-cost variant. Each variant runs through the same eval pipeline; we'll provide side-by-side dashboards. Rollout recommendation will be based on the scorecard and cost tradeoffs.
[05:38] Priya Patel: About data handling — we need to confirm where logs and KV cache live. We can't persist PHI in logs.
[05:45] Maya Lopez: We'll configure ephemeral caches for the POC and ensure no raw note retention in logs. We'll document the KMS and audit log setup.
[05:52] Nadia Kaur: Also need DSAR and deletion flow documented.
[05:55] Maya Lopez: We'll include a data handling appendix in the POC doc.
[05:59] Ava Chen: Ok, next practical steps: we'll circulate the quality eval plan and golden prompt templates by Friday (2026-10-24). You (Priya) will provide anonymized sample notes and 50 golden pairs by Monday (2026-10-26). Diego will prepare the benchmark harness and run a 7-day scheduled benchmark with daily snapshots.
[06:18] Evan Ross: On the benchmark run, can we get the raw logs? We need p95/p99 traces and per-document outputs.
[06:24] Diego Martins: Yes, we'll share per-doc outputs and a summary CSV. For privacy we'll redact PHI in shared artifacts unless we use VPC.
[06:32] Priya Patel: If the initial run looks promising, we would discuss Dedicated capacity and a longer pilot in Q1.
[06:37] Ava Chen: Noted. Any other questions?
[06:39] Priya Patel: One more: how are hallucination false positives handled in scoring? If the detector flags something but clinician disagrees, do we re-label?
[06:47] Diego Martins: Good question. We'll include a human-in-the-loop adjudication step: flagged items go to clinician review; adjudication results update gold labels and final scores (we'll version the gold set).
[06:58] Samir Joshi: That helps. Also include a brief spec for prompt injection checks?
[07:03] Ava Chen: We'll add a prompt-injection checklist to the eval plan — e.g., control tokens, limit external tool calling, and a small adversarial prompt set in regression tests.
[07:14] Priya Patel: Sounds complete.
[07:16] Ava Chen: I'll recap next steps and owner responsibilities in email. Thanks everyone.

--- End transcript ---
